original.target_description: Study 3: description identifies perceived AI authorship (AI score) versus trustworthiness within the primed condition (Figure 5, pp. 8–9); supplied Table 3 locator instead identifies profile-type and experimental-condition regressions. Target correspondence remains unresolved.

n.sample_role: Target-specific analytic N unresolved; Table 3 candidate N=2,080 denotes pooled profile-rating observations across all four conditions, not an established primed-only model N.
n.exclusions: Study 3 recruited 323 participants and excluded 115 using manipulation checks/filtering; four failing an additional manipulation check were retained. These whole-study participant counts do not establish primed-only analytic N.
n.location: pp. 7–8, Participants; p. 8, Table 3 N row; pp. 8–9, primed-condition analysis

es.location: p. 8, Table 3, “AI” x Primed condition row; pp. 8–9, Figure 5 and accompanying text
es.quote: “AI” x Primed condition        -4.976∗        2.028   -4.976∗∗∗       1.464 ... relationship between AI score and trustworthiness. Figure ... 5 shows the means and confidence intervals of ratings in ... the primed condition plotted over the associated AI scores.

notes: Identity independently verified from canonical title page: AI-Mediated Communication: How the Perception that Profile Text was Written by AI Affects Trustworthiness; Maurice Jakesch, Megan French, Xiao Ma, Jeffrey T. Hancock, Mor Naaman; CHI 2019; DOI 10.1145/3290605.3300469. Supplied text is a primary conference paper with pages 1–13 including results, references and appendices, not an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF was supplied (source_pdf_path null), so no rendering was possible or attempted. Target mapping: the neutral description identifies a continuous perceived-authorship/AI-score relationship within the primed condition, discussed with Figure 5. That section gives means, confidence intervals graphically and descriptive SDs, but no printed regression coefficient for this continuous relationship. Table 3 instead models assigned AI-like versus human-like profile type and treatment across four conditions. Candidate printed B=-4.976 occurs for the “AI” x Primed condition interaction in Model 1 (SE 2.028; one star, p<0.05) and Model 2 (SE 1.464; three stars, p<0.001); these significance bounds apply to their respective interaction models, not to an AI-score slope. They are not assigned as the target coefficient. Table 3 labels coefficients B and does not explicitly state standardisation in the inspected text; no assumption of unstandardised identity or effect conversion is made. Candidate N=2,080 is explicitly printed for each pooled Table 3 model. Participants rated 10 profiles each; this is a profile-rating observation count and is not the primed-condition participant count. No primed-only analytic N is explicitly given in the accompanying target section. No N derived from df, recruitment minus exclusions, or candidate pooled N. No arithmetic derivation performed. Unassigned replication, p and reported_success are blank placeholders.
